US Federal Reserve Holds Interest Rates Steady Ahead of Midterm Elections

29 Oct 2026, 09:24 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

Image: www.theguardian.com — Creative Commons

Key takeawaysThe US Federal Reserve voted to leave interest rates unchanged on Wednesday, opting for a pause during its final board meeting before the upcoming midterm elections. The decision keeps rates at one of the highest pre-election levels observed in more than two decades, ma

The US Federal Reserve voted to leave interest rates unchanged on Wednesday, opting for a pause during its final board meeting before the upcoming midterm elections. The decision keeps rates at one of the highest pre-election levels observed in more than two decades, maintaining the target range established following last month's hike to between 3.75% and 4%.

Board Dynamics and Inflation Context

While the central bank ultimately chose to pause, the decision was not unanimous. According to the Fed board's official statement, two out of the 12 board members dissented, preferring a quarter-point rate increase at this meeting.

The pause arrives as annualized inflation has hovered above the Fed’s 2% target for years, remaining above 3% for the majority of this year. September data showed inflation ticking upward to 3.7%, compared with 3.4% in August. Economists note that much of this year's rising price pressure has been driven by supply shocks, specifically conflicts in the Middle East involving Iran and the resulting closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which pushed oil prices briefly above $117 a barrel earlier in the week.

Fed Chair Addresses Political Independence

Speaking to reporters at a Wednesday afternoon press conference, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh addressed the timing of the decision relative to the impending midterms.

“Politics played no role in the decision,” Warsh said. “I didn’t hear an utterance about politics.”

When asked about broader political pressures, including comments from political figures regarding the composition of the board, Warsh declined to comment directly on specific remarks, though he characterized the internal deliberations as “a heck of a family fight.” He emphasized that the central bank remains focused on price stability, adding that upcoming incoming data will guide future policy choices.

Practical Implications and User Impact

Interest rates directly dictate borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, influencing the interest charged on credit cards, mortgages, and certain savings accounts. When inflation is elevated, central banks traditionally raise rates to help cool demand and slow price increases. However, economic experts point out that monetary policy has limited efficacy against supply-driven inflation, such as energy shocks stemming from geopolitical conflict.

Nicholas Economides, a professor of economics at the NYU Stern Business School, noted that the timing made radical policy action unlikely ahead of the vote, observing that the broader economy would not have had time to adjust before voters head to the polls.

Future Schedule Changes

During Wednesday's announcements, Warsh also outlined structural modifications to the Fed's meeting calendar. Beginning in the fall of 2027, the central bank will reduce its interest-rate-setting meetings from eight to seven annually, further dropping to six meetings per year by 2028, with the remaining sessions designated for broader monetary policy discussions.

Verified Facts vs. Unknowns

  • Confirmed: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates steady in a range of 3.75% to 4% following a board vote where two members dissented in favor of a quarter-point hike.
  • Confirmed: Annualized inflation has remained above 3% for most of the year, with September inflation registering at 3.7%.
  • Confirmed: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh stated that politics played no role in the decision and announced upcoming reductions to the total number of annual rate-setting meetings beginning in late 2027.
  • Unknown: The exact trajectory of future rate hikes for the remainder of the year, though multiple Fed officials have previously indicated room for further adjustments.

Readers can verify the official statements and review board documentation directly through the [The Guardian source report](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/28/fed-interest-rates-midterms).
